title: Demonstrators clash with police in Paris over living costs and public services
seoTitle: Paris protests over living costs and services

tea.why: Protesters are demonstrating against the rising cost of living, declining purchasing power, and conditions in public services and schools.
tea.want: Demonstrators want better economic conditions, improved public services, and changes to government spending and education policies.
tea.changed: Oct 18: French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez stated that roughly 550,000 to 800,000 people participated nationwide, with extensive arrests and clashes.

summary: Demonstrations regarding the cost of living, education conditions, and public services escalated into widespread unrest, arson, and looting across Paris and multiple other French cities including Marseille, Bordeaux, Lille, Lyon, and Limoges. Initially stemming from weeks of student protests over school conditions and teacher shortages, the movement broadened ahead of the upcoming presidential election. Clashes broke out between protesters and security forces, with authorities deploying tear gas, water cannons, and conducting thousands of arrests. Historic buildings, town halls, and commercial businesses were damaged or set ablaze, and a synagogue in Paris was vandalized. French President Emmanuel Macron and Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu condemned the violence, with officials noting extreme intensity in urban centers and warning of legal consequences and local curfews.
demands: Improve living costs and purchasing power
Address school conditions and teacher shortages
Better public services and government spending
response: According to French authorities, police deployed tear gas and water cannons while making thousands of arrests. President Emmanuel Macron condemned the violence, warning that offenders would be prosecuted, and Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced plans for partial local curfews.

crowd.text: approximately 550,000 people participated in the protests, while the CGT trade union put the figure at 800,000

injuries.text: more than 150 police officers were injured

updates.text: Protests and clashes broke out across Paris and multiple French cities regarding living costs and public services.
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu called on local authorities to implement partial curfews as unrest continued.
President Emmanuel Macron rejected Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez's resignation offer amidst ongoing fallout from the riots.
